packages.label: כָּבוֹד וּמַלְכוּת וְצֶדֶק
packages.reason: Torah #131 opens with the injunction to fear and dread כבוד (honor/glory) because it is a great danger. The Rebbe's first conceptual move is to equate כבוד with מלכות: 'כָּבוֹד הוּא בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת הַדָּן אֶת הַכֹּל' (Honor is a bechina of Kingship, which judges all things — citing Psalm 24:7 'מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד'). In line 3, the Rebbe continues: 'צֶדֶק מַלְכוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כָּבוֹד, מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד כַּנַּ"ל' — identifying צדק as מלכותא קדישא (holy kingship, the standard Zoharic equation of the sefirah Malkhut with the name צדק), and then identifying this entire cluster as a bechina of כבוד. The phrase 'שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת כָּבוֹד' is unambiguous bechina language. The מאזני צדק (scales of justice) then become the weighing instrument of this holy-kingship/honor — it is through כבוד/מלכות/צדק that every person is weighed and judged. These three concepts — כבוד (honor/glory), מלכות (kingship), and צדק (justice / holy kingship) — share the same essential nature: they are three faces of the divine attribute of sovereign judgment. They are all expressions of the same underlying reality: God's royal glory that scrutinizes and weighs all things. The polarity is 'good' because these all refer to the holy (קדישא) dimension: צדק מלכותא קדישא, כבוד as divine glory (מֶלֶךְ הַכָּבוֹד), and מלכות as the holy attribute. The danger of כבוד discussed in the teaching is not that כבוד itself is evil — it is that receiving honor improperly can trigger the judgment of this holy sovereignty against the person. כבוד is the dominant node because the Torah is introduced as a teaching about כבוד specifically, and all other equivalences are anchored to it.
